For investors, the discussions could give major miners access to Venezuelan coal without requiring them to acquire the mines outright. They also come as the U.S. seeks greater access to Venezuela’s mineral resources, broadening its interest in the country beyond oil.

Glencore and Peabody are working together on a potential bid involving coal assets in Venezuela’s Zulia state, according to Bloomberg News, which cited people familiar with the discussions. Investment firm Heeney Capital is separately considering a bid with Alabama-based coal producer Drummond Co.

The possible agreements have centered on giving the companies operational control and rights to purchase production rather than transferring ownership of the mines, according to the report. Such a structure could provide access to coal supplies while limiting the capital required for outright acquisitions.

The interest comes amid a broader U.S. effort to expand access to Venezuela’s mineral wealth. Reuters reported earlier this month that the Trump administration was seeking a larger U.S. role in the country's natural-resource industries beyond petroleum.

Any expansion of mining activity would take place against significant infrastructure challenges. Venezuela continues to face severe electricity shortages, with Reuters reporting Wednesday that only about 40% of the country's installed generating capacity is operating, complicating plans for new energy and industrial projects.

title: Glencore, Peabody are said to explore Venezuela coal deals
